title: App profile passwords: logout, disable, exit and uninstall, per platform

prose.text: An app profile can require a password before a user logs out of, disables, exits or uninstalls Client Connector. {{optional-passwords}}

prose.label: Platform differences.
prose.text: {{macos-zdx}} {{linux-logout-uninstall}} {{ios-passcode}} {{ios-passwords}} {{android-passwords}} {{windows-exit-through-3-5}} What happens to a password the API sets on a platform whose app profile has no such field is open {{gap:ui-gate-per-os}}.

prose.label: Other passwords in the profile.
prose.text: {{fail-close-password}} {{revert-password}} {{cli-disable-passwords}} Anti-tampering, which stops users from killing the app rather than asking for a password, is in [[zcc.app-profiles.advanced-settings:anti-tampering]].

prose.label: When a change reaches the device.
Per device instead.
prose.text: Each device's one-time passwords can stand in for these: [[zcc.passwords-and-otp.otp:otp-meanings]]. Support-side settings are in [[zcc.support-options]].

prose.label: Open questions.
prose.text: The Python SDK writes macOS passwords under snake_case keys, not the camelCase keys it reads, and what the API does with them is open {{gap:macos-password-key-asymmetry}}; the model's read and write keys are [[zcc.sdk-python.wire-keys:mac-read-write-asymmetry]]. How a password reads back through the API, and whether an empty value removes the gate, is open {{gap:password-read-and-clear}}.

ui-gate-per-os.title: What a password set through the API does on a platform whose app profile lacks it
ui-gate-per-os.detail: The question was which disable, logout and uninstall gates exist per platform: the Python SDK's five per-platform sub-policy models all carry disable, logout and uninstall password fields. The portal's per-platform lists now answer which passwords each app profile offers (iOS has no uninstall password; Android's applies only up to 3.8). What remains open is whether a value written through the API for a password the platform does not offer is stored, ignored or enforced.
ui-gate-per-os.blocks: relying on an API-set uninstall password for iOS or current Android clients
ui-gate-per-os.resolution: Partly answered by the portal's per-platform password lists (claims optional-passwords, macos-zdx, linux-logout-uninstall, ios-passcode, ios-passwords and android-passwords here).

macos-password-key-asymmetry.title: What the API does with the snake_case macOS password keys the Python SDK writes
macos-password-key-asymmetry.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the Python `MacOSPolicy` model reads `disablePassword`, `logoutPassword` and `uninstallPassword` but its `request_format()` emits `disable_password`, `logout_password` and `uninstall_password`, so a read-modify-write can move the macOS password between keys. The wire half is answered by the code: `web_policy_edit` passes the body through `zcc_to_wire(body, WebPolicy)`, which resolves each snake_case key through the field map traced from the model's `request_format()` and recurses into `mac_policy` with `MacOSPolicy`, so the macOS passwords go out as `disable_password`, `logout_password` and `uninstall_password`, not the camelCase keys the model reads. What the API does with those snake_case keys is still open. The web policy wire-key layer belongs with the app profile and web policy subjects.
macos-password-key-asymmetry.blocks: setting or rotating macOS app profile passwords through the Python SDK

password-read-and-clear.title: How app profile passwords read back through the API, and what an empty value does
password-read-and-clear.detail: Unverified legacy statements: the passwords are not stored in plain text in snapshots, read back as empty strings and are replaced on write; setting one to empty removes the gate; there is no password history or rotation enforcement, and a new value takes effect at the next policy sync. The portal shows each password with a view icon, and the password read call returns app profile passwords for a user and OS type, so the first statement is doubtful.
password-read-and-clear.blocks: rotating passwords through the API and auditing which profiles have a gate
